metadata.title: Who holidays where
metadata.source: Hand-compiled. Ratings are a judgement call, not a statistic.
metadata.rating: 0 not notable, 1 light, 3 heavy, 5 the defining crowd of the place
metadata.properties: british, german, french and spanish are each 0-5. spanish means Spanish domestic holidaymakers.
metadata.scope: Spain and Portugal: resorts, plus the cities tourists actually go to.

properties.name: Benidorm
properties.note: British archetype, but half the high-rises are full of Spaniards from Madrid.

properties.name: Magaluf
properties.note: Stag and hen capital. Germans are three miles east and never meet them.

properties.name: Platja de Palma
properties.note: Ballermann. The German Magaluf, down to the beer steins and schlager.

properties.name: Palmanova
properties.note: Magaluf's quieter neighbour. Only just.

properties.name: Alcúdia
properties.note: Family end of the market, tilting German. Old town worth the detour.

properties.name: Cala d'Or
properties.note: Whitewashed calas, German package trade, very quiet by ten.

properties.name: Sant Antoni de Portmany
properties.note: The West End strip. Sunset Strip is the tolerable half.

properties.name: Ibiza Town
properties.note: The one genuinely pan-European crowd on this map.

properties.name: Ciutadella
properties.note: Menorca stayed low-rise and mostly Spanish and British.

properties.name: Torremolinos
properties.note: Where the package holiday was invented. Faded, cheerful, still busy.

properties.name: Benalmádena
properties.note: Arroyo de la Miel and the marina. Bars showing the football.

properties.name: Fuengirola
properties.note: Long beach, long-standing British and Finnish contingents.

properties.name: Marbella
properties.note: Money rather than lager, but Puerto Banús is Puerto Banús.

properties.name: Estepona
properties.note: The Costa del Sol town that kept its old quarter.

properties.name: Nerja
properties.note: Prettier, older crowd. Long-settled British population.

properties.name: Almuñécar
properties.note: Granada's beach. Almost entirely domestic, and all the better for it.

properties.name: Torrevieja
properties.note: Expat belt and Madrid's second home in equal measure.

properties.name: Calp
properties.note: German and Dutch lean. The Peñón is the actual draw.

properties.name: Xàbia
properties.note: Expat belt. Pleasant, and thoroughly colonised.

properties.name: Gandia
properties.note: Valencia and Madrid decamp here in August. Barely a foreign accent.

properties.name: Peñíscola
properties.note: Castle on a rock, packed with Spanish families and Aragonese plates.

properties.name: Benicàssim
properties.note: Domestic beach town that borrows a British crowd for festival week.

properties.name: La Manga
properties.note: A sandbar of flats between two seas. Overwhelmingly Spanish.

properties.name: Roquetas de Mar
properties.note: Big German package presence beside a very Spanish resort town.

properties.name: Mojácar
properties.note: White hill village above a strip of British-leaning beach bars.

properties.name: Lloret de Mar
properties.note: French and Dutch coaches as much as British stag parties.

properties.name: Empuriabrava
properties.note: Canal-side marina town, an hour from the border. Effectively French.

properties.name: Roses
properties.note: The French weekend. Signs and menus follow suit.

properties.name: L'Escala
properties.note: Anchovies, Greek ruins at Empúries, and a French summer crowd.

properties.name: Cadaqués
properties.note: Dalí's village. French day-trippers and Barcelona money.

properties.name: Salou
properties.note: PortAventura feeder town. British, French and Spanish families all.

properties.name: Cambrils
properties.note: Salou's grown-up neighbour: seafood, and a domestic crowd.

properties.name: Sitges
properties.note: Barcelona's beach and a long-standing gay resort. Cosmopolitan.

properties.name: Barcelona
properties.note: Everyone. The French arrive by train in numbers nobody counts.

properties.name: San Sebastián
properties.note: Twenty minutes from France, and it shows all summer.

properties.name: Hondarribia
properties.note: Border town. Half the terrace is over from Hendaye for lunch.

properties.name: Zarautz
properties.note: Surf beach with a Spanish and French crowd, no package trade.

properties.name: Santander
properties.note: Where Madrid goes to escape August. Sardinero is all domestic.

properties.name: Llanes
properties.note: Green coast, cider, and Spanish families who booked last October.

properties.name: Gijón
properties.note: A working city with a beach, and almost no foreign tourism.

properties.name: Sanxenxo
properties.note: Galicia's summer capital. Madrid and Galicia, nobody else.

properties.name: A Coruña
properties.note: Glass balconies, good food, and a domestic crowd.

properties.name: Conil de la Frontera
properties.note: Seville and Madrid in August. Atlantic wind keeps the package trade off.

properties.name: Zahara de los Atunes
properties.note: Tuna, dunes, and a well-heeled Spanish crowd.

properties.name: Chiclana
properties.note: Novo Sancti Petri is where German package holidays go on the Atlantic.

properties.name: Tarifa
properties.note: Kitesurfing brings the Germans; the wind keeps everyone else away.

properties.name: El Puerto de Santa María
properties.note: Sherry, tuna and a Sevillano summer crowd.

properties.name: Gibraltar
properties.note: Not a resort, actually British. Marks and Spencer and monkeys.

properties.name: Granada
properties.note: The Alhambra draws every nationality on this map at once.

properties.name: Jaca
properties.note: Ski and mountain town. Spanish, with French over the pass.

properties.name: Albufeira
properties.note: The Strip. Portugal's answer to Benidorm.

properties.name: Praia da Rocha
properties.note: Portimão's beach strip. Cliffs are genuinely good, crowd is not.

properties.name: Lagos
properties.note: Backpackers and surfers alongside the package crowd.

properties.name: Vilamoura
properties.note: Golf and marina. Sedate, moneyed, entirely inauthentic.

properties.name: Valencia
properties.note: City break boom: Fallas, paella and a growing British stag trade.

properties.name: Madrid
properties.note: Everyone passes through. August belongs to whoever stayed behind.

properties.name: Bilbao
properties.note: The Guggenheim, and the French over for the weekend.

properties.name: Málaga
properties.note: The Costa del Sol's city, and lately the reason people skip the resorts.

properties.name: Porto
properties.note: Port lodges and cheap flights. As busy as Valencia, on half the residents.

properties.name: Lisbon
properties.note: Tuk-tuks in Alfama. The city that ran out of long lets.

properties.name: Santiago de Compostela
properties.note: Pilgrims of every nationality, and Spanish ones in the greatest number.

properties.name: Seville
properties.note: French city breaks in spring, everyone else in the shade by July.
